insight_text: Audience demand is clustering around recession-risk explainers that connect market stress, layoffs, and household finance decisions.
High-performing videos frame the economy as an urgent decision problem rather than a broad news update.
Some recession angles spike quickly and fade when they rely on alarm without a practical viewer action.
Policy headlines perform best when creators translate the budget impact into immediate stock-market scenarios.
Viewers are rewarding videos that explain what investors may do next after fiscal announcements.
Generic budget summaries are weakening unless they include a clear market implication or portfolio angle.
Positioning content is gaining when it contrasts cash, stocks, bonds, and defensive sectors in one decision frame.
Creators are seeing traction by turning uncertainty into a checklist for what viewers should review now.
Rotation predictions can fail when the video does not anchor the claim to visible market evidence.
Retirement strategy content is outperforming when it answers a specific account-choice question for beginners.
ETF allocation explainers are pulling steady interest when paired with age, risk, or contribution context.
Broad retirement tips are weakening because they lack a concrete decision point for the viewer.
Small-cap ideas gain attention when the thesis is narrow, timely, and framed around overlooked upside.
Ranked watchlists work when creators explain why the market may be mispricing each stock.
Ticker-only hype is a failed breakout pattern unless it is supported by a durable business catalyst.
